claims.notes: RECIPE (agent card). BUILD: (1) Compose the manifest JSON with camelCase keys — required top-level fields are `format`, `version`, `definition`, `profile`, `memory` (agent_snapshot.rs:164-174). Set format exactly to "buzz-agent-snapshot" and version to 1 (agent_snapshot.rs:59-63, validated at 387-399). `definition.name` and `profile.displayName` must be non-empty after trim (agent_snapshot.rs:400-405). `memory` must be `{"level":"none"}` — level "none" with a non-empty `entries` array is rejected before any write (import.rs:285-294). (2) Base64-encode (STANDARD alphabet) the raw JSON bytes; that base64 string is the tEXt chunk TEXT (agent_snapshot.rs:324, decoded at 368-370 with `.trim()` tolerance). (3) Build any valid PNG whose pixels are the avatar you want, and insert one tEXt chunk with keyword `buzz_agent_snapshot`, i.e. chunk payload = b"buzz_agent_snapshot" + 0x00 + <base64> (keyword/NUL layout asserted at media_snapshot_png.rs:37-41 and validation.rs:584-589). (4) Placement is load-bearing: the chunk must come BEFORE IDAT — the reference writer inserts it immediately after IHDR, because the `png` crate reader used on import only surfaces text chunks seen before IDAT (media_snapshot_png.rs:54-58; inject helper at 59-80). (5) Keep the image within 2048x2048 or the import errors out, and keep the re-encoded body under 2 MiB or the body simply will not be adopted as the avatar (snapshot_avatar.rs:6, 18-23, 35-37). Keep total file under 10 MiB (import.rs:234-239). DETECTION: the app reads the first 4 bytes; `[0x89,0x50,0x4e,0x47]` routes to the PNG branch, anything else to JSON — the filename is never consulted for this (import.rs:213, 232-233, 219). It then calls `extract_chunk_payload_png` (agent_snapshot.rs:354-371), which uses `Decoder::read_info()` and searches `uncompressed_latin1_text` for keyword == "buzz_agent_snapshot", base64-decoding the text. The decoded JSON is probed for its `format` field: "buzz-agent-snapshot" -> Plain, the locked discriminator -> Locked, anything else or missing -> error (agent_snapshot_envelope.rs:174-195). Finally, if `profile.avatarDataUrl` is absent, the PNG pixels are adopted as the avatar (import.rs:242-261). For a `.team.png`, substitute keyword `buzz_team_snapshot`, format "buzz-team-snapshot", and the TeamSnapshot shape `{format, version, team{name,...}, members[]}` (team_snapshot.rs:49, 52, 76-87). SEPARATE GATE if the PNG is uploaded through Buzz media: the relay-side validator permits exactly ONE tEXt chunk and only with an allowlisted snapshot keyword; a second snapshot chunk or any other tEXt/eXIf/zTXt/iTXt/iCCP chunk is rejected as forbidden metadata (validation.rs:592-625).

extra_findings:
Additional context found while verifying, not requested but load-bearing for anyone acting on this:

1. LOCKED CARDS. A second chunk-payload variant shares the same `buzz_agent_snapshot` tEXt keyword: an encrypted NIP-44 envelope. `parse_chunk_payload` (desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/agent_snapshot_envelope.rs:174-196) dispatches on the JSON `format` string, so the same PNG keyword can carry either plaintext or ciphertext. Locked envelopes have their own size cap applied BEFORE typed deserialization (`MAX_LOCKED_ENVELOPE_JSON_BYTES`, lines 181-187) and fail closed with `LOCKED_CARD_REFUSAL` when neither of the envelope's two key endpoints is held locally (import.rs:318-333). The PNG-body-to-avatar override at import.rs:242-261 deliberately does NOT run for locked payloads.

2. SANITIZER ROUND-TRIP. Uploading a snapshot PNG through Buzz media would normally destroy the chunk, because the upload sanitizer re-encodes. desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/media_snapshot_png.rs:22-80 extracts the raw chunk (length+type+payload+CRC) before the re-encode and re-injects it immediately after IHDR afterwards; the CRC stays valid because the chunk bytes are unchanged (comment at lines 54-58). The extractor walks chunk structure manually rather than decoding the image, so a malformed file yields None and falls through to normal sanitization. Entry point is desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/media.rs:267.

3. RELAY-SIDE STRICTNESS is tighter than the desktop reader. crates/buzz-media/src/validation.rs:592-646 permits exactly one tEXt chunk with an allowlisted keyword and rejects everything else, including pHYs, which is explicitly excluded as an identity channel (comment at lines 626-628). So a PNG the desktop importer accepts may still be rejected on upload if it carries extra ancillary chunks.

4. EXPORT-SIDE BODY SELECTION. desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/personas/snapshot.rs:313-315 and `resolve_png_body_avatar_bytes` at :333+ choose the PNG body separately from the manifest avatar source, so the body and the manifest avatar can intentionally differ (this is what makes trading cards work). desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/personas/card.rs:872-889 downsizes the manifest avatar to 512 px so the tEXt chunk stays small.

5. TEAM PATH ASYMMETRY. Team snapshots have no envelope/locked variant and no body-avatar adoption — the body is always the 1x1 placeholder (team_snapshot.rs:128-144), and each member's avatar rides inside that member's own AgentSnapshot.
